state:
Goal `core-signal-and-4-more`. `Core\Signal`, `Core\Signature` and `Core\SignedCookie` are green.
`Core\Socket::current`, `::receive`, `::send` and `::sendBytes` now have all their feature proofs:
an `about.md`, three examples, one attack and one bench each, plus Rust tests carrying `covers:` in
`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/socket.rs`. `Core\Socket` has a class card and is off
`CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`; the four member cards are in the plain voice. They run a real
connection through `nvs run --peer <file>`, the scripted WebSocket peer this session added
(`crates/nvs-cli/src/peer.rs` owns the `.nvsp` format; `docs/examples/README.md` § *A WebSocket
peer* is the reader's half). No attack found a runtime bug. Still red in stage 2:
`Core\Socket::upgrade` (everything but the card) and all of `Core\Socket\Message`.

next.title: the dossier
next.note: one file set: `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/socket.rs`, its proof trees under `core/Socket/` and `core/Socket-Message/`, and `nvs run`'s `--peer` and `--request` doors in `crates/nvs-cli/src/main.rs`.

items.text: **`Core\Socket\Message::text`, `::bytes`, `::value`, and `Core\Socket\Message`'s class card** — each owes `about.md`, three examples, one attack, one bench and two tests. A `.nvsp` peer gives `text` and `bytes` their frames, and a `Core\Topic::publish` inside the same script gives `value` a delivery (the `Core\Socket` examples show both). The Rust test `receive_answers_a_peer_frame_and_a_topic_delivery_from_one_wait` reads all four slots and only needs `covers:` lines. Write the class card above `MESSAGE` and delete `Core\Socket\Message` from `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD` in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs`. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/socket.rs:476`

**`Core\Socket::upgrade`** — owes examples, hostile, perf and a Rust `covers:` marker (the upgrade tests from `an_upgrade_leaves_the_resolvers_program_and_a_copy_of_its_argument_in_the_slot` onward call the member and only need the line). A CLI run offers no `nvs_runtime::UpgradeSlot`, so every upgrade throws there. The next step is to have `nvs run --request` offer a slot when the `.nvsr` carries `Upgrade: websocket`, and then run the prepared script with the `.nvsp` peer beside it, the way `nvs_server::serve_connection` offers one. That is a harness change, like `--peer`; it is not a language change. `rule:concurrency/an-upgrade-is-spawn-shaped`. `crates/nvs-cli/src/main.rs:2510`

backlog: `Core\Sse` and `Core\Topic` owe every example, attack and bench; `nvs run --peer` gives `Core\Topic` a subscriber, and `Core\Sse` needs the same kind of harness for its stream (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/sse.rs`).
A connection script's `echo` goes to standard output under `--peer`, where a served connection's goes to the socket; `crates/nvs-cli/src/peer.rs`'s module doc says what the harness prints.
